items.eu-ai-act::article-4: Providers and deployers of AI systems shall take measures to ensure, to their best extent, a sufficient level of AI literacy of their staff and other persons dealing with the operation and use of AI systems on their behalf, taking into account their technical knowledge, experience, education and training and the context in which the systems are used.
items.eu-ai-act::article-5: Prohibited outright in the EU: social scoring by or on behalf of public authorities, real-time remote biometric identification in publicly accessible spaces for law enforcement (narrow exceptions), untargeted scraping of facial images, emotion recognition in workplaces and education, and predictive policing based solely on profiling.
items.eu-ai-act::article-8: High-risk AI systems must meet the requirements of Section 2 of Chapter III taking into account their intended purpose as specified in the provider's instructions for use, promotional or sales materials, and technical documentation, as well as the generally acknowledged state of the art on AI; the Article 9 risk management system must be taken into account when ensuring compliance. Where a product contains a high-risk AI system to which the requirements of this Regulation and of the Union harmonisation legislation listed in Section A of Annex I apply, the provider is responsible for ensuring the product is fully compliant with all applicable requirements and may integrate the necessary testing, reporting, and documentation into the procedures already required under that legislation.
items.eu-ai-act::article-9: Providers of high-risk AI systems shall implement a risk management system, maintain data governance and technical documentation, ensure transparency, human oversight, and accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity across the lifecycle.
items.eu-ai-act::article-10: Training, validation and testing data for high-risk AI systems shall be relevant, sufficiently representative, and to the best extent possible error-free and complete, considering the areas in which the system is used.
items.eu-ai-act::article-11: The technical documentation of a high-risk AI system shall be drawn up before placing it on the market and kept up to date, sufficient to assess the system's compliance with the Act's requirements.
items.eu-ai-act::article-12: High-risk AI systems shall technically allow for the automatic recording of events (logs) over the lifetime of the system, with logging capabilities enabling recording of events relevant to the system's traceability and functioning appropriate to its intended purpose.
items.eu-ai-act::article-13: High-risk AI systems shall be designed and developed with sufficient transparency so that providers can supply information about their purpose, characteristics, capabilities and limitations, and so that deployers can understand the system's operation and use it appropriately.
items.eu-ai-act::article-14: High-risk AI systems shall be designed with measures to enable human oversight, so that natural persons can prevent, correct or halt system outputs that may cause harmful or discriminatory effects.
items.eu-ai-act::article-15: High-risk AI systems shall achieve an appropriate level of accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity throughout their lifecycle, and shall be resilient to errors, faults or inconsistencies that may arise internally or in the environment in which they operate.
items.eu-ai-act::article-16: Providers of high-risk AI systems shall ensure their systems comply with the Chapter III Section 2 requirements; put a quality management system in place; maintain the technical documentation and the automatically generated logs; carry out the applicable conformity assessment before placing the system on the market or putting it into service; draw up the EU declaration of conformity and affix the CE marking; register the system as required; and take any necessary corrective action.
items.eu-ai-act::article-17: Providers of high-risk AI systems shall put in place a documented quality management system ensuring compliance with this Regulation, covering at least a regulatory-compliance strategy; design, design-control and verification techniques; development, quality-control and quality-assurance techniques; examination, test and validation procedures before, during and after development; the technical specifications, including standards, to be applied and the means to ensure compliance where harmonised standards are not applied in full; systems and procedures for data management; the risk management system referred to in Article 9; the post-market monitoring plan referred to in Article 72; procedures for reporting serious incidents under Article 73; communication and record-keeping procedures; resource management including security-of-supply measures; and an accountability framework for management and staff, with implementation proportionate to the provider's organisation.
items.eu-ai-act::article-62: When the fees for conformity assessment under Article 43 are set, the specific interests and needs of SME providers, including start-ups, must be taken into account, and those fees reduced proportionately to the provider's size, market size and other relevant indicators.
items.eu-ai-act::article-63: Microenterprises within the meaning of Recommendation 2003/361/EC may comply with certain elements of the quality management system required by Article 17 of this Regulation in a simplified manner, provided that they do not have partner enterprises or linked enterprises within the meaning of that Recommendation. For that purpose, the Commission shall develop guidelines on the elements of the quality management system which may be complied with in a simplified manner considering the needs of microenterprises, without affecting the level of protection or the need for compliance with the requirements in respect of high-risk AI systems. Paragraph 1 shall not be interpreted as exempting those operators from fulfilling any other requirements or obligations laid down in this Regulation, including those established in Articles 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 72 and 73.
items.eu-ai-act::article-18: Providers of high-risk AI systems shall keep, for a period ending 10 years after the high-risk AI system has been placed on the market or put into service, at the disposal of the national competent authorities: the technical documentation referred to in Article 11; the documentation concerning the quality management system referred to in Article 17; the documentation concerning changes approved by notified bodies, where applicable; the decisions and other documents issued by notified bodies, where applicable; and the EU declaration of conformity referred to in Article 47. Each Member State shall determine the conditions under which the documentation remains at the disposal of the national competent authorities for that period if a provider or its authorised representative established on its territory ceases activity before the end of the period, and providers that are financial institutions subject to internal-governance documentation requirements under Union financial services law shall maintain the technical documentation as part of the documentation kept under that law.
items.eu-ai-act::article-19: Providers of high-risk AI systems shall keep the logs automatically generated by their systems and referred to in Article 12 (1), to the extent such logs are under their control, for a period appropriate to the intended purpose of at least six months, unless provided otherwise in applicable Union or national law; providers that are financial institutions subject to requirements regarding their internal governance, arrangements or processes under Union financial services law shall maintain those automatically generated logs as part of the documentation kept under the relevant financial services law.
items.eu-ai-act::article-20: Providers of high-risk AI systems who consider or have reason to consider that a high-risk AI system they have placed on the market or put into service is not in conformity with this Regulation shall immediately take the necessary corrective actions to bring the system into conformity, to withdraw it, disable it, or recall it, as appropriate, and shall inform the distributors, and where applicable the deployers, the authorised representative and the importers accordingly. Where the high-risk AI system presents a risk within the meaning of Article 79 (1) and the provider becomes aware of that risk, the provider shall immediately investigate the causes, in collaboration with the reporting deployer where applicable, and inform the market surveillance authorities competent for the system concerned and, where applicable, the notified body that issued a certificate for the system in accordance with Article 44, in particular of the nature of the non-compliance and of any relevant corrective action taken.
items.eu-ai-act::article-21: Providers of high-risk AI systems shall, upon a reasoned request by a competent authority, provide that authority all the information and documentation necessary to demonstrate the conformity of the system with the requirements set out in Section 2 of this Chapter, in a language easily understood by the authority in one of the official languages of the institutions of the Union as indicated by the Member State concerned. Upon a reasoned request by a competent authority, providers shall also give the requesting authority, as applicable, access to the automatically generated logs of the high-risk AI system referred to in Article 12 (1), to the extent such logs are under their control. Any information obtained by a competent authority pursuant to this Article shall be treated in accordance with the confidentiality obligations set out in Article 78.
items.eu-ai-act::article-22: Providers of high-risk AI systems established in a third country shall, by written mandate, appoint an authorised representative established in the Union before placing such a system on the Union market, and shall enable that representative to perform the obligations and procedures established by this Regulation on its behalf. The authorised representative shall perform the tasks specified in the mandate, provide a copy of the mandate to market surveillance authorities upon request, and be empowered to carry out tasks including verifying that the EU declaration of conformity referred to in Article 47 and the technical documentation referred to in Article 11 exist and that an appropriate conformity assessment procedure has been carried out, keeping the required documentation at the disposal of the competent authorities for ten years after the system has been placed on the market or put into service, providing a competent authority upon a reasoned request with the information and documentation necessary to demonstrate conformity, cooperating in any action taken in relation to the system, and, where applicable, complying with the registration obligations referred to in Article 49 (1). The authorised representative shall terminate the mandate if it considers or has reason to consider the provider to be acting contrary to its obligations under the Regulation, and shall immediately inform the relevant market surveillance authority and, where applicable, the relevant notified body of the termination and the reasons for it.
items.eu-ai-act::article-23: Importers shall place a high-risk AI system on the market only after verifying that the relevant conformity assessment procedure referred to in Article 43 has been carried out by the provider, that the provider has drawn up the technical documentation in accordance with Article 11 and Annex IV, that the system bears the required CE marking and is accompanied by the EU declaration of conformity referred to in Article 47 and the instructions for use, and that the provider has appointed an authorised representative in accordance with Article 22 (1). Where an importer has sufficient reason to consider that a system is not in conformity with this Regulation, is falsified, or is accompanied by falsified documentation, it shall not place the system on the market until it has been brought into conformity, and where the system presents a risk within the meaning of Article 79 (1) it shall inform the provider, the authorised representative, and the market surveillance authorities. Importers shall indicate their name, registered trade name or trade mark, and contact address on the system, its packaging, or accompanying documentation; ensure that storage or transport conditions under their responsibility do not jeopardise compliance with the requirements set out in Section 2; keep, for 10 years after the system has been placed on the market or put into service, a copy of the certificate issued by the notified body, where applicable, and the instructions for use and the EU declaration of conformity referred to in Article 47; provide the competent authorities, upon a reasoned request, with all necessary information and documentation to demonstrate conformity and ensure the technical documentation can be made available; and cooperate with the competent authorities in any action taken in relation to a system they have placed on the market, in particular to reduce and mitigate the risks posed by it.
items.eu-ai-act::article-24: Distributors shall make a high-risk AI system available on the market only after verifying that it bears the required CE marking, is accompanied by a copy of the EU declaration of conformity referred to in Article 47 and the instructions for use, and that the provider and the importer, as applicable, have complied with their respective obligations as laid down in Article 16, points (b) and (c), and Article 23(3). Where a distributor considers or has reason to consider, on the basis of the information in its possession, that the system is not in conformity with the requirements set out in Section 2, it shall not make the system available on the market until it has been brought into conformity, and where the system presents a risk within the meaning of Article 79(1), it shall inform the provider or the importer to that effect. Distributors shall ensure that, while a high-risk AI system is under their responsibility, storage or transport conditions do not jeopardise their compliance with the requirements set out in Section 2. Distributors that consider or have reason to consider a high-risk AI system they have made available on the market not to be in conformity with this Regulation shall take the corrective actions necessary to bring that system into conformity, to withdraw it or recall it, or shall ensure that the provider, or any relevant operator, as appropriate, takes those measures, and where the system presents a risk within the meaning of Article 79(1), they shall immediately inform the provider or the importer of the system and the authorities competent for the high-risk AI system concerned, giving details, in particular, of the non-compliance and of any corrective actions taken. Upon a reasoned request from a relevant competent authority, distributors shall provide that authority with all the information and documentation regarding their actions necessary to demonstrate the conformity of that system with the requirements set out in Section 2, and shall cooperate with the relevant competent authorities in any action those authorities take in relation to a high-risk AI system made available on the market by them, in particular to reduce or mitigate the risk posed by it.
items.eu-ai-act::article-25: Any distributor, importer, deployer or other third party that makes a high-risk AI system available on the Union market shall be considered the provider of that system, and subject to the provider obligations under Article 16, where they put their name or trademark on a high-risk AI system already placed on the market, make a substantial modification to it that affects its compliance or results in a modification of the intended purpose for which it has been assessed, or modify the intended purpose of an AI system, including a general-purpose AI system, that has not been classified as high-risk in such a way that it becomes a high-risk AI system in accordance with Article 6. Where those circumstances occur, the initial provider shall no longer be considered the provider of that specific system and shall closely cooperate with the new provider, making available the necessary information and the reasonably expected technical access and other assistance required for the fulfilment of the obligations of this Regulation, in particular regarding compliance with the conformity assessment of high-risk AI systems; this duty does not apply where the initial provider has clearly specified that its system is not to be changed into a high-risk AI system and therefore does not fall under the obligation to hand over the documentation. In the case of high-risk AI systems that are safety components of products covered by the Union harmonisation legislation listed in Section A of Annex I, the product manufacturer shall be considered the provider, and be subject to the obligations under Article 16, where the system is placed on the market together with the product under the manufacturer's name or trademark, or put into service under that name or trademark after the product has been placed on the market. The provider of a high-risk AI system and any third party that supplies an AI system, tools, services, components, or processes used or integrated in a high-risk AI system shall, by written agreement, specify the necessary information, capabilities, technical access and other assistance, based on the generally acknowledged state of the art, to enable the provider to fully comply with the obligations of this Regulation; this does not apply to third parties making such tools, services, processes or components, other than general-purpose AI models, accessible to the public under a free and open-source licence. The change-of-provider and safety-component duties are without prejudice to the need to observe and protect intellectual property rights, confidential business information and trade secrets in accordance with Union and national law.
items.eu-ai-act::article-26: Deployers of high-risk AI systems shall take appropriate technical and organisational measures to use the systems in accordance with the provider's instructions for use, and shall assign effective human oversight to persons with the necessary competence, training and authority; to the extent a deployer controls the input data, it shall ensure that data is relevant and sufficiently representative for the intended purpose.
items.eu-ai-act::article-27: Deployers that are bodies governed by public law, or private entities providing public services, and deployers of the high-risk AI systems referred to in Article 6(2) and listed in points 5(b) and (c) of Annex III (excluding those intended to be used in the area listed in point 2 of Annex III), shall perform an assessment of the impact on fundamental rights that the use of the system may produce, prior to placing the system into service. The assessment shall describe the deployer's processes and conditions of use per the provider's instructions for use and technical documentation, the period and frequency of use, the categories of natural persons and groups likely to be affected, the specific risks of harm to those categories taking account of the information given by the provider pursuant to Article 13, the implementation of human oversight measures, and the measures to be taken if those risks materialise, including internal governance and complaint mechanisms. The obligation applies to the first use of the system; in similar cases the deployer may rely on previously conducted fundamental rights impact assessments or existing assessments carried out by the provider, and shall update the information where an element of paragraph 1 has changed or is no longer up to date. Once the assessment has been performed, the deployer shall notify the market surveillance authority of its results, submitting the filled-out template as part of the notification; deployers may be exempt from that duty in the case referred to in Article 46(1). If obligations under this Article are already met through a data protection impact assessment conducted pursuant to Article 35 of Regulation (EU) 2016/679 or Article 27 of Directive (EU) 2016/680, the fundamental rights impact assessment shall complement that data protection impact assessment.
items.eu-ai-act::article-42: Providers of high-risk AI systems may rely on two presumptions of conformity under this Article: a system trained and tested on data reflecting the specific geographical, behavioural, contextual or functional setting within which it is intended to be used is presumed to comply with the relevant requirements of Article 10(4); and a system certified, or for which a statement of conformity has been issued, under a cybersecurity scheme pursuant to Regulation (EU) 2019/881 whose references have been published in the Official Journal of the European Union is presumed to comply with the cybersecurity requirements of Article 15, in so far as the certificate or statement of conformity covers those requirements.
items.eu-ai-act::article-43: Before placing a high-risk AI system on the market, providers shall carry out the applicable conformity assessment (Article 43), draw up an EU declaration of conformity (Article 47) and affix the CE marking (Article 48); most high-risk systems may be assessed by internal control, with third-party assessment for certain systems.
items.eu-ai-act::article-44: Notified bodies shall draw up certificates, in accordance with Annex VII, in a language that can be easily understood by the relevant authorities in the Member State in which the notified body is established. A certificate shall be valid for the period it indicates, which shall not exceed five years for AI systems covered by Annex I and four years for AI systems covered by Annex III; at the request of the provider, its validity may be extended for further periods of the same length based on a re-assessment carried out in accordance with the applicable conformity assessment procedures, and any supplement to a certificate shall remain valid provided the certificate it supplements is valid. Where a notified body finds that an AI system no longer meets the requirements set out in Section 2, it shall, taking account of the principle of proportionality, suspend, withdraw or restrict the certificate unless compliance is ensured by appropriate corrective action taken by the provider within an appropriate deadline set by the notified body, which shall give reasons for its decision. An appeal procedure against decisions of the notified bodies, including on conformity certificates issued, shall be available.
items.eu-ai-act::article-46: By way of derogation from Article 43, a market surveillance authority may, on a duly justified request and for exceptional reasons of public security or the protection of life and health of persons, environmental protection or the protection of key industrial and infrastructural assets, authorise the placing on the market or putting into service of a specific high-risk AI system in the Member State concerned for a limited period while the necessary conformity assessment procedures are being carried out, provided the authority concludes the system complies with the requirements of Chapter III, Section 2; those procedures must be completed without undue delay. In a duly justified situation of urgency for exceptional reasons of public security, or in the case of a specific, substantial and imminent threat to the life or physical safety of natural persons, law-enforcement or civil protection authorities may put such a system into service without prior authorisation provided authorisation is requested during or after the use without undue delay; if the request is refused, the use must stop immediately and all results and outputs be discarded. Authorisations are notified to the Commission and the other Member States and are deemed justified if no objection is raised within 15 calendar days; for systems related to products under Union harmonisation legislation listed in Section A of Annex I, only the derogations established in that legislation apply.
items.eu-ai-act::article-47: Before placing a high-risk AI system on the market, the provider shall draw up a machine-readable, physical or electronically signed EU declaration of conformity for each such system and keep it at the disposal of the national competent authorities for 10 years after the system has been placed on the market or put into service; the declaration shall state that the system meets the requirements set out in Section 2, contain the information set out in Annex V, be translated into a language easily understood by the competent authorities of the Member States concerned, and be submitted to the relevant authorities upon request; where the system is also subject to other Union harmonisation legislation requiring an EU declaration of conformity, a single declaration may be drawn up covering all applicable Union law; by drawing up the declaration the provider assumes responsibility for compliance, and shall keep it up-to-date as appropriate.
items.eu-ai-act::article-48: The provider must affix the CE marking to indicate that the high-risk AI system meets the requirements of Chapter III, Section 2 and other applicable Union harmonisation legislation providing for it. The marking shall be affixed visibly, legibly and indelibly; where that is not possible or warranted by the nature of the system, it may be affixed to the packaging or to the accompanying documentation. For systems provided digitally, a digital CE marking may be used only if it can be easily accessed via the interface from which the system is accessed or via an easily accessible machine-readable code or other electronic means. Where a notified body carried out the Article 43 conformity assessment procedures, the marking shall be followed by the notified body's identification number, affixed by the body itself or, under its instructions, by the provider or the provider's authorised representative, and that number shall also be indicated in any promotional material mentioning that the system fulfils the requirements for CE marking.
items.eu-ai-act::article-49: Before placing on the market or putting into service for first use, providers or, where applicable, authorised representatives of high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III, with the exception of systems referred to in point 2 of Annex III, shall register themselves and their system in the EU database referred to in Article 71; providers shall likewise register systems they have concluded are not high-risk under Article 6(3), deployers that are public authorities shall register themselves and the use of the system in the EU database, and registration of law-enforcement, migration, asylum and border-control systems shall be in a secure non-public section of the database accessible only to the Commission and the national authorities referred to in Article 74(8).
items.eu-ai-act::article-71: The EU database for high-risk AI systems set up by the Commission in collaboration with the Member States holds the registration data of Article 49 and Article 60 systems: the data listed in Sections A and B of Annex VIII is entered by the provider or, where applicable, its authorised representative, and the data listed in Section C by deployers that are public authorities, agencies or bodies; the information registered under Article 49 is publicly accessible in a user-friendly, machine-readable manner except for the secure sections referred to in Article 49(4) and Article 60(4), point (c), while information registered under Article 60 is accessible only to market surveillance authorities and the Commission unless the provider consents to public access.
items.eu-ai-act::article-72: Providers of high-risk AI systems shall implement a post-market monitoring system proportionate to the system's risks and intended purpose, to systematically gather and analyse information on the performance of the system throughout its lifetime, documented using the technical documentation (Annex IV).
items.eu-ai-act::article-73: Providers of high-risk AI systems placed on the Union market shall report to the market surveillance authorities of the Member States where the incident occurred any serious incident that directly or indirectly leads to a person's death or serious health harm, a serious and irreversible disruption of critical infrastructure, or an infringement of Union law protecting fundamental rights (Article 3, point 49). Reports shall be made immediately once a causal link is established or reasonably likely, and in any event not later than 15 days after the provider or, where applicable, the deployer becomes aware of the incident; within 2 days in the event of a widespread infringement or an incident as defined in Article 3, point 49(b); and within 10 days where a person has died. An incomplete initial report may be followed by a complete one. The provider shall then investigate the incident without delay, including a risk assessment and corrective action, and cooperate with the competent authorities and any notified body concerned.
items.eu-ai-act::article-50: Providers shall ensure that AI systems intended to interact directly with natural persons are designed and developed so that the natural persons concerned are informed that they are interacting with an AI system, unless this is obvious from the point of view of a reasonably well-informed, observant and circumspect natural person, taking into account the circumstances and the context of use.
items.eu-ai-act::article-53: Providers of general-purpose AI models shall draw up and keep up-to-date technical documentation of the model, including its training and testing process and the results of its evaluation, containing at minimum the elements set out in Annex XI; make available information and documentation to providers of AI systems who intend to integrate the model, containing at minimum the elements set out in Annex XII; put in place a policy to comply with Union law on copyright and related rights, including to identify and comply with reservations of rights expressed pursuant to Article 4(3) of Directive (EU) 2019/790; and draw up and make publicly available a sufficiently detailed summary about the content used for training of the model. The documentation duties do not apply to models released under a free and open-source licence allowing access, usage, modification, and distribution, whose parameters, including weights, architecture, and usage information, are made publicly available, except for models with systemic risks.
items.eu-ai-act::article-54: Providers of general-purpose AI models established in third countries shall, prior to placing a model on the Union market, appoint by written mandate an authorised representative established in the Union, and shall enable that representative to perform and carry out on their behalf the obligations and procedures established by the Regulation. The mandate shall empower the authorised representative to verify that the technical documentation specified in Annex XI has been drawn up and that the obligations under Article 53 and, where applicable, Article 55 have been fulfilled by the provider; to keep a copy of that technical documentation and the provider's contact details at the disposal of the AI Office and national competent authorities for a period of 10 years after the model has been placed on the market; to provide the AI Office, upon a reasoned request, with all information and documentation necessary to demonstrate compliance with the obligations in Chapter V; to cooperate with the AI Office and competent authorities, upon a reasoned request, in any action they take in relation to the model, including when it is integrated into AI systems placed on the market or put into service in the Union; and to be addressed, in addition to or instead of the provider, on all issues related to ensuring compliance with the Regulation. The authorised representative shall perform the tasks specified in the mandate, provide a copy of the mandate to the AI Office upon request, and terminate the mandate if it considers or has reason to consider the provider to be acting contrary to its obligations, informing the AI Office immediately of the termination and the reasons. The obligation does not apply to providers of models released under a free and open-source licence allowing access, usage, modification, and distribution, whose parameters, including weights, architecture, and usage information, are made publicly available, unless the models present systemic risks.
items.eu-ai-act::article-51: A general-purpose AI model shall be classified as a general-purpose AI model with systemic risk if it has high-impact capabilities evaluated on the basis of appropriate technical tools and methodologies, including indicators and benchmarks, or if the Commission decides, ex officio or following a qualified alert from the scientific panel, that the model has capabilities or an impact equivalent to those indicated by those criteria, having regard to the criteria set out in Annex XIII. The model is presumed to have high-impact capabilities when the cumulative amount of computation used for its training, measured in floating point operations, is greater than 10^25. Meeting either condition triggers the provider's notification procedure under Article 52; the Commission may amend the thresholds and supplement the benchmarks and indicators by delegated acts under Article 97 so that they continue to reflect the state of the art.
items.eu-ai-act::article-52: A provider of a general-purpose AI model that meets the high-impact-capability condition in Article 51(1)(a) shall notify the Commission without delay and in any event within two weeks after the requirement is met or it becomes known that it will be met, including the information necessary to demonstrate that the requirement has been met. Together with the notification, the provider may present sufficiently substantiated arguments to demonstrate that, exceptionally, due to the model's specific characteristics, it does not present systemic risks and should not be classified as a general-purpose AI model with systemic risk; where the Commission concludes those arguments are not sufficiently substantiated it shall reject them and the model shall be considered to present systemic risk. Upon a reasoned request containing objective, detailed, and new reasons, a provider whose model has been designated by the Commission on the basis of the criteria in Annex XIII may obtain a reassessment of the designation, at the earliest six months after the designation decision or after any decision to maintain it.
items.eu-ai-act::article-55: In addition to their obligations under Articles 53 and 54, providers of general-purpose AI models that present systemic risk shall perform model evaluations in accordance with standardised protocols and tools reflecting the state of the art, including conducting and documenting adversarial testing of the model to identify and mitigate systemic risks; assess and mitigate possible systemic risks at Union level, including their sources, that may stem from the development, the placing on the market, or the use of such models; keep track of, document, and report without undue delay to the AI Office and, as appropriate, to national competent authorities, relevant information about serious incidents and possible corrective measures; and ensure an adequate level of cybersecurity protection for the model and the physical infrastructure of the model. Providers may rely on codes of practice within the meaning of Article 56 to demonstrate compliance until a harmonised standard is published, compliance with which grants presumption of conformity; providers not adhering to an approved code of practice or a harmonised standard shall demonstrate alternative adequate means of compliance for assessment by the Commission.
items.eu-ai-act::article-59: Within an AI regulatory sandbox established under Article 57, personal data lawfully collected for other purposes may be processed solely for developing, training and testing AI systems in the sandbox under regulatory supervision and pursuant to an approved sandbox plan, in accordance with Article 59, only where all of the following cumulative conditions are met: the AI systems are developed by a public authority or another natural or legal person for safeguarding substantial public interest in one or more of the areas of public safety and health, environmental protection and the green transition, energy sustainability, safety and resilience of transport systems and critical infrastructure, or the efficiency of public administration and services; the personal data are necessary to comply with requirements in Chapter III, Section 2 that cannot effectively be fulfilled with anonymised, synthetic or other non-personal data; effective monitoring and response mechanisms exist to identify, mitigate and if necessary stop high risks to the rights and freedoms of data subjects, as referred to in Article 35 of Regulation (EU) 2016/679 and Article 39 of Regulation (EU) 2018/1725; the data are processed in a functionally separate, isolated and protected environment under the control of the prospective provider, with access limited to authorised persons; originally collected data may be further shared only in accordance with Union data protection law and data created in the sandbox cannot be shared outside it; the processing neither leads to measures or decisions affecting the data subjects nor affects their rights under Union data protection law; personal data are protected by appropriate technical and organisational measures and deleted once sandbox participation ends or their retention period expires; logs of the processing are kept for the duration of participation unless Union or national law provides otherwise; a complete and detailed description of the process and rationale behind training, testing and validation is kept with the testing results as part of the technical documentation referred to in Annex IV; and a short summary of the project is published on the competent authority's website, excluding sensitive operational data of law enforcement, border control, immigration or asylum authorities. For criminal-justice and public-security purposes under the control of law enforcement authorities, such processing must be based on specific Union or national law subject to the same cumulative conditions. Article 59 is without prejudice to other Union or national law governing personal-data processing, in compliance with Union data protection law.
items.eu-ai-act::article-60: Testing of high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III in real-world conditions outside AI regulatory sandboxes may be conducted by providers or prospective providers in accordance with Article 60 and an accompanying real-world testing plan, without prejudice to the prohibitions under Article 5. Such testing may take place at any time before the system is placed on the market or put into service in the Union, on the provider's own or in partnership with one or more deployers, and is without prejudice to any ethical review required by Union or national law. Testing may proceed only where all the conditions of Article 60(4) are met, including: a real-world testing plan submitted to, and approved by (expressly or tacitly after thirty days), the market surveillance authority of the Member State concerned; registration of the testing in the EU database in accordance with Article 71(4) with a unique single identification number and the information listed in Annex IX; establishment in the Union of the provider or an appointed legal representative; safeguards for any transfer of testing data to third countries; a duration no longer than necessary and as a rule no more than six months, extendable once; appropriate protection of subjects belonging to vulnerable groups; informed consent of the subjects in accordance with Article 61, or, in the case of law enforcement, where seeking informed consent would prevent the AI system from being tested, that the testing and its outcome have no negative effect on the subjects and that their personal data are deleted after the test; provision of the relevant instructions for use under Article 13 and a written agreement on roles and responsibilities where deployers participate; effective oversight by suitably qualified persons; and predictions, recommendations or decisions of the system that can be effectively reversed and disregarded. Subjects may withdraw from the testing at any time by revoking their informed consent without detriment or justification and may request the immediate and permanent erasure of their personal data. Member States shall confer on their market surveillance authorities, in accordance with Article 75, the powers to require information and to carry out checks on the conduct of the testing. Any serious incident identified in the course of the testing shall be reported to the national market surveillance authority in accordance with Article 73, and the provider shall adopt immediate mitigation measures or suspend or terminate the testing, establishing a procedure for the prompt recall of the system upon termination. Providers or prospective providers shall notify the national market surveillance authority of the suspension or termination of the testing and of its final outcomes, and are liable under applicable Union and national liability law for any damage caused in the course of the testing.
items.eu-ai-act::article-61: Before any subject may participate in testing in real-world conditions under Article 60, the provider or prospective provider shall obtain their freely-given informed consent, after being duly informed with concise, clear, relevant, and understandable information regarding: (a) the nature and objectives of the testing and the possible inconvenience linked to participation; (b) the conditions under which the testing is to be conducted, including the expected duration of the subjects' participation; (c) their rights and guarantees regarding participation, in particular the right to refuse to participate in, and to withdraw from, testing at any time without any resulting detriment and without having to provide any justification; (d) the arrangements for requesting the reversal or the disregarding of the predictions, recommendations or decisions of the AI system; and (e) the Union-wide unique single identification number of the testing in real-world conditions in accordance with Article 60(4), point (c), and the contact details of the provider or its legal representative from whom further information can be obtained. The informed consent shall be dated and documented and a copy shall be given to the subjects of testing or their legal representative.
items.eu-ai-act::article-80: Where a market surveillance authority has sufficient reason to consider that an AI system classified by the provider as non-high-risk pursuant to Article 6(3) is indeed high-risk, it shall carry out an evaluation of the system's classification based on the conditions set out in Article 6(3) and the Commission guidelines. Where the evaluation finds that the system is high-risk, the authority shall require the relevant provider to take all necessary actions to bring the system into compliance with the requirements and obligations laid down in the Regulation, and to take appropriate corrective action, within a period it may prescribe. The provider shall ensure that all necessary action is taken to bring the system into compliance; where the provider fails to do so within that period, the provider is liable to fines in accordance with Article 99, and shall further ensure that all appropriate corrective action is taken in respect of all the systems concerned made available on the Union market. Where the provider does not take adequate corrective action within that period, Article 79(5) to (9) shall apply. Where an evaluation establishes that the provider misclassified the system as non-high-risk in order to circumvent the application of the requirements in Chapter III, Section 2, the provider is likewise liable to fines in accordance with Article 99.
items.eu-ai-act::article-82: Where a market surveillance authority, having evaluated a high-risk AI system under Article 79 and consulted the relevant national public authority under Article 77(1), finds that although the system complies with the Regulation it nevertheless presents a risk to the health or safety of persons, to fundamental rights, to other aspects of public interest protection, it shall require the relevant operator to take all appropriate measures so that the system no longer presents that risk without undue delay, within a prescribed period. The provider or other relevant operator shall ensure corrective action is taken in respect of all the systems concerned made available on the Union market within the timeline prescribed by the authority; Member States shall inform the Commission and other Member States of any such finding.
items.eu-ai-act::article-83: Where a market surveillance authority of a Member State finds that the CE marking has been affixed in violation of Article 48 or has not been affixed, that the EU declaration of conformity referred to in Article 47 has not been drawn up or has not been drawn up correctly, that the registration in the EU database referred to in Article 71 has not been carried out, that, where applicable, no authorised representative has been appointed, or that technical documentation is not available, it shall require the relevant provider to put an end to the non-compliance concerned within a period it may prescribe. Where the non-compliance persists, the authority shall take appropriate and proportionate measures to restrict or prohibit the high-risk AI system being made available on the market or to ensure that it is recalled or withdrawn from the market without delay.
items.eu-ai-act::article-85: Without prejudice to other administrative or judicial remedies, any natural or legal person having grounds to consider that there has been an infringement of the provisions of this Regulation may submit a complaint to the relevant market surveillance authority. In accordance with Regulation (EU) 2019/1020, such complaints shall be taken into account for the purpose of conducting market surveillance activities, and shall be handled in line with the dedicated procedures established therefor by the market surveillance authorities.
items.eu-ai-act::article-86: Where a decision is taken on the basis of the output of a high-risk AI system listed in Annex III and produces legal effects or similarly significant effects on a person, that person shall have the right to obtain from the deployer clear and meaningful explanations of the role of the AI system in the decision-making procedure and of the main elements of the decision taken.
